Too p2w for my tastes, extremely slow otherwise. Usually a freemium game will at least be fun to free players for the first few days, this one you almost immediately hit a wall of "sit and wait" within a few hours.

'My Singing Monsters' is a creatively distinctive entry in the world-building genre, revolving around the unique hook of musical synchronization. Unlike standard "farming" simulators, every creature added to the player's island contributes its own vocal or instrumental layer to a growing, harmonious song. This mechanic provides a genuine sense of progression, as the simple rhythm of a single monster eventually evolves into a complex, multi-layered orchestral performance. The character designs are charmingly bizarre, and the satisfaction of unlocking a new "part" of the song creates a rewarding audio-visual loop that is both relaxing and uniquely memorable.

However, the experience is heavily tethered to the "freemium" mechanics typical of mobile-first titles, which can significantly slow down the pace of play. Progression often becomes a test of patience, as breeding rare monsters or clearing obstacles requires long real-time waiting periods or the use of premium currency to expedite. While the game is entirely playable for free, the late-game grind and the constant presence of microtransaction prompts can detract from the whimsical atmosphere. Ultimately, it is a highly charming and creative musical sandbox that is perfect for casual play, provided the player is comfortable navigating the inherent friction of its time-gated systems.

citations.review_text: Ive come back to this game at least every couple months for the past couple years and its always been fun rediscovering the game and whats new! The community and development behind the team is really awesome and although the core gameplay can be a little tedious at times (as to be expected with waiting games) and is certainly not a game for everyone, the collection and decoration aspect can be really cool and obviously the actual music of the game is really good (my favourite tracks being wublin island, water island and mech islet).

It's a nice, fun, relaxing game.
+The songs are actually not too bad, with some going incredibly hard.
+The monster designs are all unique, and the rare/epic skins for some of them are really cool-looking.
It's a game that relies heavily on grinding however, since lot's of things cost a lot of coins (in the millions),  and this goes for the same with all the other currencies (there's like 6 I think).
If you just want to relax and hear some music then this game's for you :D

I initially left a "not recommended" review.
But then, it turned out that the things I like about this game were enough to keep me logging in for 100+ hours, in spite of what frustrates me about it.
I also realised I would probably recommend it to some of my friends.
So honesty dictates I should change my rating.

Let me first get into why I had selected "not recommended" initially, because this still really bugs me.
Everything you do in this game runs on a timer - breeding, incubating, upgrading facilities, baking treats so you can level your monsters, removing obstacles so you can decorate your islands...
As you progress in the game, the timers become longer. Right now, most of my timers are between 10 and 36 hours.
In practice, this means that you log in, collect what came of your previous timers, and start new timers. There's a couple of mini games you can play. And then you hit a hard wall where there is nothing for you to do but wait for your timers to end.
You can use a resource called diamonds to end your timers early. Diamonds can be collected in the game but not in great quantities, and there is no way to grind them indefinitely (so you kinda have a daily cap, though it varies a bit day by day). 
This is a great source of frustration for me because I'd love to be able to play this game for a few hours in a row on the weekends. And also because there is an easy way the developers could have alleviated this.
There is a combat system in the game, which currently doesn't bring very exciting rewards. All they would have had to do was create an engine that generates random teams of monsters aligned with the level of yours, and then assign a diamond reward if you win. That way instead of logging out, you could stay in the game and do combat to earn some diamonds.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe recent minigame or clubbox events as functioning like gambling, relying on luck to obtain exclusive or limited-time monsters with tickets or tokens that are difficult to earn without spending money.

citations.review_text:
I've played this game for a long time and have many hours logged. I've bought all the DLC packs, limited-time costumes, etc. Long-time fan for several years (I started playing over a decade ago). It pains me to write this but I don't know where else I can possibly garner the devs' attention.

The new minigame system is truly just remarkably egregious. You need "minigame tokens" to participate in a limited-time event to obtain limited-time monsters. You earn these tokens through events or by purchasing them with 1 diamond with a 2-hour cooldown. Which means, without spending any real money, you're limited on the amount of minigame tokens you can earn through gameplay.

The thing with the minigame is that the rewards (specifically the limited-time monsters) are completely random. There's no rhyme or reason to what you'll get, not even a pity system it seems. It totally comes down to luck on whether you get the new monsters or not.

Because the only reliable way to get more tokens is actually buying them, this means the system is basically gambling. It's essentially a gacha game at this point, just without any sort of pity system. 

There are several possible fixes they could implement. They could give each level clear set rewards, so you know what you're getting and are guaranteed the monsters after X games, or they could lift the artificial 2-hour cooldown on buying the tokens with diamonds. I'd even be willing to spend up to 10 diamonds per token.

The FOMO this event brings is just insane. It's disappointing that even with over 17,000 diamonds (the main premium currency in this game), there's nothing I can do to get the new monsters except spend money (which, as I stated earlier, I *am* willing to spend money on this game, just not on what's essentially a gacha).

I'll change this review once meaningful change is done to this event. The current system is unacceptable.

well i was going to give this a recommendation because i have 200 hours in this game and i love aspects of it to death but im gonna be honest the fact that the clubbox has introduced two cool new gameplay elements that are literally just gambling has me seriously rethinking that. 

both have you gambling for exclusive rewards that are increasingly excruciatingly difficult to get unless you feel like spending a huge amount of money on the absurdly overpriced tickets. both of these, in my opinion as someone with zero interest in spending upwards of fifty dollars on gambling per clubbox act, got old really quickly. gambling simply feels bad and it feels like both the tickets that i've earned and my real life time are being wasted here. i do not play my singing monsters to gamble and would quite it if the game would stop pushing me to do so.

so ok just ignore them, right? i like the rest of the game just fine so i can just ignore the gambling and it'll be problem solved, right? well the thing is the main way you get tickets/cards is through regular gameplay, and whenever you earn them, you get a whooole full screen popup about it. it's frequent, it's intrusive, it halts the entire game so you can look at the cards you got (even if you skip the pack opening cutscene) or how many tickets you got or whatever other rewards are interspersed in between, and there is no option to disable this. so even if you ignore the event, truly choosing to not engage with the event is simply not an option. you do not get to opt out.

so ok say you do decide to spend money. in the case of the clubbox act rewards themselves, which you get directly from spending tickets, you are guaranteed to get all the rewards eventually - any amount of hype generated slowly but surely drags you to the end. no such luck with the cards, though, from what i can tell /those/ are totally random, and there's no pity system beyond being able to save up stars gotten from duplicate cards for extra packs, whi…
